title: Impact of Obesity Diagnosis on Medication Use

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) is appropriate here since treatment (obesity diagnosis) is assigned based on a clear cutoff rule at a specific BMI threshold. The key assumption is that individuals just above and below the BMI cutoff are similar in all unobservable characteristics except for the treatment assignment, allowing us to estimate the local average treatment effect at the discontinuity.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(rdrobust)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s100_data.csv")

# Identify the cutoff point (where treatment status changes)
cutoff <- min(data$running_var[data$treated == 1])
print(paste("Cutoff identified at BMI:", cutoff))

# Center the running variable around the cutoff
data$bmi_centered <- data$running_var - cutoff

# Main RDD analysis using rdrobust
rdd_result <- rdrobust(y = data$y, 
                      x = data$bmi_centered, 
                      c = 0)

# Print main results
print("=== MAIN RDD RESULTS ===")
print(summary(rdd_result))
cat("\nTreatment Effect (LATE):", round(rdd_result$coef[1], 4))
cat("\nStandard Error:", round(rdd_result$se[1], 4))
cat("\nP-value:", round(rdd_result$pv[1], 4))
cat("\nConfidence Interval: [", round(rdd_result$ci[1,1], 4), ",", round(rdd_result$ci[1,2], 4), "]\n")

# Robustness checks
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===\n")

# 1. Different bandwidths
bw_half <- rdrobust(data$y, data$bmi_centered, h = rdd_result$bws[1]/2)
bw_double <- rdrobust(data$y, data$bmi_centered, h = rdd_result$bws[1]*2)

cat("Half bandwidth effect:", round(bw_half$coef[1], 4), "(SE:", round(bw_half$se[1], 4), ")\n")
cat("Double bandwidth effect:", round(bw_double$coef[1], 4), "(SE:", round(bw_double$se[1], 4), ")\n")

# 2. Different polynomial orders
rdd_quad <- rdrobust(data$y, data$bmi_centered, p = 2)
cat("Quadratic specification effect:", round(rdd_quad$coef[1], 4), "(SE:", round(rdd_quad$se[1], 4), ")\n")

# 3. Check for manipulation (McCrary density test)
density_test <- rddensity(data$bmi_centered)
cat("Density test p-value:", round(density_test$test$p_jk, 4), "\n")

# Visualization
png("rdd_plot.png", width = 800, height = 600)
rdplot(data$y, data$bmi_centered, 
       title = "RDD: Effect of Obesity Diagnosis on Medication Use",
       x.label = "BMI (centered at cutoff)",
       y.label = "Log Medication Use")
dev.off()

cat("\nPlot saved as rdd_plot.png\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive treatment effect of approximately 0.3-0.6 in log medication use, representing a 35-80% increase in medication use following an obesity diagnosis. This positive effect is anticipated because: (1) obesity diagnosis typically triggers medical interventions and prescription medications for weight management, diabetes prevention, or cardiovascular health; (2) the diagnosis may increase patient awareness and healthcare utilization; and (3) physicians are more likely to prescribe preventive medications once the obesity threshold is crossed. The effect should be statistically significant given the clear clinical significance of the obesity cutoff in medical practice.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare medication use for individuals just above and below the BMI cutoff.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Receiving an obesity diagnosis at the BMI cutoff leads to increased medication use.
